functions.name: sxt_init
functions.description: Initialize the library and select the compute backend. Call once before using any other API. Returns 0 on success, nonzero on failure.
requirements: Must be called exactly once before any other function that requires the backend.
config must point to a valid struct sxt_config.
config->backend should be one of SXT_GPU_BACKEND or SXT_CPU_BACKEND (per documentation).
Nonzero return value indicates initialization failure and callers should not proceed.

functions.name: sxt_curve25519_compute_pedersen_commitments
functions.signature: void sxt_curve25519_compute_pedersen_commitments(struct sxt_ristretto255_compressed* commitments, uint32_t num_sequences, const struct sxt_sequence_descriptor* descriptors, uint64_t offset_generators);
functions.description: Compute Pedersen commitments for multiple sequences using internally generated curve25519 (ristretto255) generators with an offset. Each commitments[i] is the product over j of g_{offset_generators + j} ^ a_ij. Skips computation if num_sequences == 0.
requirements: Library backend must be initialized via sxt_init.
descriptors must not be NULL.
commitments must not be NULL when num_sequences > 0.
For each descriptors[i], element_nbytes must be a power of 2 with 1 <= element_nbytes <= 32 (per struct comment).
For each descriptors[i], if n > 0 then data must not be NULL and encodes little-endian elements of size element_nbytes.
descriptors[i].is_signed may be set; if signed then element_nbytes must be <= 16 (per struct comment).
Abnormal termination occurs if any listed invalid condition is met.

num_sequences == 0 skips computation.
Abnormal termination occurs if any listed invalid condition is met.

functions.name: sxt_ristretto255_get_generators
functions.signature: int sxt_ristretto255_get_generators(struct sxt_ristretto255* generators, uint64_t offset_generators, uint64_t num_generators);
functions.description: Fill an array with num_generators pre-specified pseudo-random Ristretto255 generators starting at the given index offset. Returns 0 on success, nonzero on error. If num_generators == 0, computation is skipped.
requirements: If num_generators > 0, generators must not be NULL.
offset_generators is applied as a shift to the generator index sequence.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates failure.

functions.name: sxt_curve25519_get_one_commit
functions.signature: int sxt_curve25519_get_one_commit(struct sxt_ristretto255* one_commit, uint64_t n);
functions.description: Compute the nth Ristretto point defined as the identity when n == 0, otherwise the sum of the first n generators g[0] + ... + g[n-1] as defined by sxt_ristretto255_get_generators with offset 0. Writes the result to one_commit. Returns 0 on success, nonzero on error.
requirements: one_commit must not be NULL.
n selects the number of generators to sum; behavior otherwise follows the definition provided.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates failure.

functions.name: sxt_curve25519_prove_inner_product
functions.signature: void sxt_curve25519_prove_inner_product(struct sxt_ristretto255_compressed* l_vector, struct sxt_ristretto255_compressed* r_vector, struct sxt_curve25519_scalar* ap_value, struct sxt_transcript* transcript, uint64_t n, uint64_t generators_offset, const struct sxt_curve25519_scalar* a_vector, const struct sxt_curve25519_scalar* b_vector);
functions.description: Create a non-interactive inner product proof over Ristretto255 using a strobe transcript, with generators derived from sxt_ristretto255_get_generators(offset, 2^ceil(log2(n))). Produces arrays l_vector and r_vector of length ceil(log2(n)) and a final scalar ap_value. Transcript is updated with proof elements and challenges.
requirements: transcript must not be NULL.
ap_value must not be NULL.
a_vector must not be NULL and must have length n.
b_vector must not be NULL and must have length n.
n must be non-zero.
If n is non-zero, l_vector and r_vector must not be NULL and must each have space for ceil(log2(n)) compressed points.
generators_offset selects the base index for the generator sequence used in the proof.
Abnormal termination occurs if any listed invalid condition is met.

functions.name: sxt_curve25519_verify_inner_product
functions.signature: int sxt_curve25519_verify_inner_product(struct sxt_transcript* transcript, uint64_t n, uint64_t generators_offset, const struct sxt_curve25519_scalar* b_vector, const struct sxt_curve25519_scalar* product, const struct sxt_ristretto255* a_commit, const struct sxt_ristretto255_compressed* l_vector, const struct sxt_ristretto255_compressed* r_vector, const struct sxt_curve25519_scalar* ap_value);
functions.description: Verify a Ristretto255 inner product proof against bases derived from sxt_ristretto255_get_generators(offset, 2^ceil(log2(n))). Uses the provided transcript, public vector b, claimed inner product <a,b>, commitment <a,G>, proof vectors L and R, and scalar ap_value. Returns 1 if the proof verifies; otherwise 0. Transcript is used/updated during verification.
requirements: transcript must not be NULL.
b_vector must not be NULL and must have length n.
product must not be NULL and must equal <a,b> used by the prover.
a_commit must not be NULL and must equal <a,G> used by the prover.
ap_value must not be NULL.
n must be non-zero.
If n is non-zero, l_vector and r_vector must not be NULL and must each have length ceil(log2(n)).
Caller must check the return value: 1 indicates verification success; 0 indicates failure.
Abnormal termination occurs if any listed invalid condition is met.

functions.name: sxt_multiexp_handle_new
functions.signature: struct sxt_multiexp_handle* sxt_multiexp_handle_new(unsigned curve_id, const void* generators, unsigned n);
functions.description: Create a handle for efficient multiexponentiations using a fixed sequence of generators for a given curve. Generators must be provided in the curve-specific projective/affine type as documented.
requirements: curve_id must identify the curve and determine the expected generator type: RISTRETTO255 -> struct sxt_ristretto255*, BLS_381 -> struct sxt_bls12_381_g1_p2*, BN_254 -> struct sxt_bn254_g1_p2*, GRUMPKIN -> struct sxt_grumpkin_p2*.
generators must point to an array of n elements of the appropriate type for the specified curve_id.
n specifies the number of generators provided.
The returned handle must later be freed with sxt_multiexp_handle_free.

functions.name: sxt_multiexp_handle_new_from_file
functions.signature: struct sxt_multiexp_handle* sxt_multiexp_handle_new_from_file(unsigned curve_id, const char* filename);
functions.description: Create a multiexponentiation handle by deserializing precomputed generator data from a file. Faster than constructing from raw generators.
requirements: curve_id selects the curve and associated generator type for the handle.
filename should reference a readable file containing a serialized handle produced by sxt_multiexp_handle_write_to_file.
The returned handle must later be freed with sxt_multiexp_handle_free.

functions.name: sxt_multiexp_handle_write_to_file
functions.signature: void sxt_multiexp_handle_write_to_file(const struct sxt_multiexp_handle* handle, const char* filename);
functions.description: Serialize and write a multiexponentiation handle to a file for later fast loading with sxt_multiexp_handle_new_from_file.
requirements: handle must be a valid multiexp handle created by sxt_multiexp_handle_new or sxt_multiexp_handle_new_from_file.
filename should be a valid writable path.
Behavior on NULL filename or I/O errors is not specified in the header (unknown).

functions.name: sxt_multiexp_handle_free
functions.description: Free resources associated with a multiexponentiation handle.
requirements: handle must be a handle previously returned by sxt_multiexp_handle_new or sxt_multiexp_handle_new_from_file.
Whether handle may be NULL is not specified (unknown).

functions.name: sxt_fixed_multiexponentiation
functions.signature: void sxt_fixed_multiexponentiation(void* res, const struct sxt_multiexp_handle* handle, unsigned element_num_bytes, unsigned num_outputs, unsigned n, const uint8_t* scalars);
functions.description: Compute one or more multiexponentiations using a handle’s fixed generators. Scalars are provided as a column-major array with element_num_bytes per scalar and dimensions n (generators) by num_outputs (outputs). Writes num_outputs group elements to res in the curve-specific type corresponding to the handle.
requirements: res must point to storage for num_outputs results of the curve-specific group element type associated with handle (see sxt_multiexp_handle_new).
handle must be a valid multiexp handle for the desired curve and generator set.
element_num_bytes specifies the number of bytes per scalar in little-endian; valid range is not specified (unknown).
n must equal the number of generators associated with handle.
scalars must not be NULL and must contain num_outputs*n scalars laid out in column-major order: s_11, s_21, ..., s_1n, s_2n, ...
num_outputs specifies how many separate multiexponentiations to compute.

functions.name: sxt_fixed_packed_multiexponentiation
functions.signature: void sxt_fixed_packed_multiexponentiation(void* res, const struct sxt_multiexp_handle* handle, const unsigned* output_bit_table, unsigned num_outputs, unsigned n, const uint8_t* scalars);
functions.description: Compute multiexponentiations where each output uses a specified bit-width for scalars, packed contiguously per generator row. The scalars buffer is packed by output according to output_bit_table and padded to a whole number of bytes per row.
requirements: res must point to storage for num_outputs results of the curve-specific group element type associated with handle.
handle must be a valid multiexp handle.
output_bit_table must point to an array of length num_outputs, where each entry specifies the number of bits for that output’s scalars.
Let bit_sum = sum(output_bit_table); the row size in bytes is ceil(bit_sum/8); scalars must contain n rows of this size in a packed column-major layout.
n must equal the number of generators associated with handle.
scalars must not be NULL and must be packed as specified.
num_outputs specifies the number of outputs to compute.

functions.name: sxt_fixed_vlen_multiexponentiation
functions.signature: void sxt_fixed_vlen_multiexponentiation(void* res, const struct sxt_multiexp_handle* handle, const unsigned* output_bit_table, const unsigned* output_lengths, unsigned num_outputs, const uint8_t* scalars);
functions.description: Compute multiexponentiations with per-output bit-widths and varying lengths. Scalars for each generator row are packed contiguously by output using output_bit_table and padded to bytes, with outputs shorter than the maximum padded with zeros. output_lengths must be sorted ascending.
requirements: res must point to storage for num_outputs results of the curve-specific group element type associated with handle.
handle must be a valid multiexp handle.
output_bit_table must point to an array of length num_outputs, where each entry specifies the number of bits for that output’s scalars.
output_lengths must point to an array of length num_outputs and must be sorted in ascending order.
Let n denote the longest output length (i.e., max(output_lengths)); scalars must contain rows sized to ceil(sum(bits)/8) with outputs packed contiguously and shorter outputs padded with zeros.
scalars must not be NULL and must be packed as specified.

functions.name: sxt_prove_sumcheck
functions.signature: void sxt_prove_sumcheck(void* polynomials, void* evaluation_point, unsigned field_id, const struct sumcheck_descriptor* descriptor, void* transcript_callback, void* transcript_context);
functions.description: Construct a sumcheck proof for a polynomial sum_i mult_i * prod_j f_j(X1,...,Xr) over a specified field. On completion, writes the round polynomials as a (round_degree+1) x num_variables column-major matrix of FIELD elements into polynomials and the evaluation point into evaluation_point. transcript_callback is invoked each round to sample a random FIELD value and has the conceptual signature void (FIELD* r, void* context, FIELD* polynomial, unsigned polynomial_length).
requirements: field_id selects the finite field used and determines the concrete FIELD type for pointers in descriptor, polynomials, evaluation_point, and callback.
descriptor must describe the sumcheck instance with FIELD-typed pointers per its documentation.
polynomials must point to writable storage for (round_degree+1) x (num_variables) FIELD elements in column-major order.
evaluation_point must point to writable storage for num_variables FIELD elements.
transcript_callback must be a function compatible with void(FIELD* r, void* context, FIELD* polynomial, unsigned polynomial_length).
transcript_context is an opaque pointer passed to transcript_callback.

data_types.description: A byte buffer interpreted as a sequence of n little-endian integers (scalars), each of fixed width element_nbytes where element_nbytes is a power of two between 1 and 32 bytes. The total buffer size is n * element_nbytes. Integers may be treated as signed or unsigned depending on a separate is_signed flag; when signed, element_nbytes is limited to <= 16. This format is used to supply scalar coefficients for multiexponentiation/Pedersen commitment computations.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces a bytes buffer intended for FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the
# sxt_curve25519_compute_pedersen_commitments fuzz stub. The stub may request up to
# n * element_nbytes bytes per sequence, where:
# - num_sequences in [0,3]
# - element_nbytes is a power of two in {1,2,4,8,16,32} (if signed, <=16)
# - n in [0,15]
# The stub will resize shorter strings with zeros, so providing sufficiently long,
# well-structured buffers increases valid coverage without relying on resizing.
#
# Strategy:
# - Construct up to 4 distinct sequences back-to-back in one buffer, so that any
#   FUZZ_PARAM_STR() call can slice an interesting region.
# - For variety, include multiple element widths and lengths, mixing signed/unsigned
#   patterns and edge-case scalar values (0, 1, -1, max, min, random) in little-endian.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_BUF = 4096

# Helper to produce little-endian integer of given width from a Python int,
# wrapping modulo 2^(8*width) to mimic field reduction size expectations.

def le_int(val: int, width: int) -> bytes:
    mask = (1 << (8 * width)) - 1
    v = val & mask
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(width):
        out.append(v & 0xFF)
        v >>= 8
    return bytes(out)

# Produce interesting scalar sequences for a given element width and signed flag.

def make_scalar_row(rng: random.Random, width: int, count: int, signed: bool) -> bytes:
    # Build a palette of interesting values respecting width and signedness.
    bits = 8 * width
    if signed:
        min_val = -(1 << (bits - 1))
        max_val = (1 << (bits - 1)) - 1
        interesting = [
            0,
            1,
            -1,
            max_val,
            min_val,
        ]
        # Add some near-boundary values if possible
        if max_val >= 2:
            interesting.extend([2, 3])
        if min_val <= -2:
            interesting.extend([-2, -3])
        # Random signed values
        for _ in range(6):
            interesting.append(rng.randint(min_val, max_val))
    else:
        max_val = (1 << bits) - 1
        interesting = [
            0,
            1,
            max_val,
        ]
        # Add bit-pattern edges
        if bits >= 2:
            interesting.extend([3, (1 << (bits - 1)), (1 << (bits - 1)) - 1])
        # Random unsigned values
        for _ in range(6):
            interesting.append(rng.randrange(0, max_val + 1))

    # Assemble count scalars cycling through interesting values and adding randomness
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(count):
        if i < len(interesting):
            v = interesting[i]
        else:
            # Mix in randoms interspersed with repeated boundary cases
            if i % 7 == 0:
                v = interesting[rng.randrange(0, min(len(interesting), 8))]
            else:
                if signed:
                    v = rng.randint(-(1 << (bits - 1)), (1 << (bits - 1)) - 1)
                else:
                    v = rng.randrange(0, (1 << bits))
        out += le_int(v, width)
    return bytes(out)

# Build one logical sequence block with header-like markers to help differentiation.
# The fuzzer stub ignores any headers; they simply provide extra bytes for slicing.

def make_sequence_block(rng: random.Random, width: int, count: int, signed: bool) -> bytes:
    # Header marker encodes width, count, signedness for diversity (not consumed by target).
    header = bytearray()
    header += b"SXT\x01"                    # magic
    header += struct.pack('<B', width)       # element_nbytes
    header += struct.pack('<B', 1 if signed else 0)
    header += struct.pack('<H', count & 0xFFFF)
    # Add some padding to vary alignment
    pad_len = rng.randrange(0, 4)
    header += bytes([0xA5]) * pad_len

    body = make_scalar_row(rng, width, count, signed)

    # Footer checksum-like bytes (unused by target)
    footer = bytearray()
    checksum = sum(body) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    footer += struct.pack('<I', checksum)

    return bytes(header) + body + bytes(footer)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide how many logical blocks to include (0..4). 0 still returns some bytes.
    num_blocks = rng.randrange(1, 5)

    # Candidate element widths; signed allowed only up to 16.
    widths = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]

    blobs: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0

    for _ in range(num_blocks):
        width = rng.choice(widths)
        signed = bool(rng.getrandbits(1)) and width <= 16
        # Choose length comparable to fuzzer cap but varied
        # Favor small and edge lengths, occasionally larger within cap
        choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15]
        count = rng.choice(choices)

        block = make_sequence_block(rng, width, count, signed)
        if total + len(block) > MAX_BUF:
            break
        blobs.append(block)
        total += len(block)

    # Ensure we have at least some scalar bytes so that need > 0 regions get content
    if not blobs:
        # Fallback minimal block: width 1, 8 elements unsigned
        blobs.append(make_sequence_block(rng, 1, 8, False))

    data = b"".join(blobs)

    # Trim to MAX_BUF just in case
    if len(data) > MAX_BUF:
        data = data[:MAX_BUF]

    return data
